title: lightweight playbook checkpointer and safe failure-replay CLI
author: Maya Alvarez
description:
Motivation: On-call responders often need a compact, reproducible snapshot of an interrupted playbook run to diagnose flaky remediation steps without re-triggering side effects. This PR introduces a lightweight checkpoint format plus a local CLI that can replay a checkpoint in a safe, non-destructive mode or step through actions with simulated side effects. The goal is faster incident triage and safer post-incident debugging while preserving oncall ergonomics and privacy controls.

What this PR delivers: 1) Playbook checkpointer (server-side): a new capability in incident-bot that can emit a compact checkpoint bundle containing: playbook step state, normalized inputs/outputs (sanitized), pointers to traces and log fragments, and a small TTL-backed storage token. Bundles are gzipped protobuf-compatible JSON to keep tooling-simple and human-inspectable. 2) failure-replay CLI: a single binary `rb-playcheck` added to the devtoolchain with subcommands: `capture`, `download`, `replay --dry-run`, `replay --interactive`, and `inspect`. Dry-run verifies control-flow without executing external remediation actions; interactive mode lets operators advance steps and optionally run the real action after an explicit confirm. 3) Telemetry prefetch hooks: when creating a checkpoint, incident-bot will register a short-lived telemetry snapshot request to the SLO toolkit collector so the CLI can fetch correlated traces/logs for local replay. 4) Safety and privacy: automatic redaction for credentials and PII, opt-in flag for full payload capture, and RBAC checks on download endpoints.

Design notes: - Checkpoint format focuses on minimal surface area: step id, status, last executor, normalized inputs, last output (truncated), error stack (sanitized), and pointer map for telemetry artifacts. TTL defaults to 48h. - The server stores bundles in the same ephemeral attachments backend; a lightweight token is returned that allows download if the requester has the right scope. - Replay simulates external calls by default. Hooks are pluggable so downstream teams can add richer simulators for specific services.

Checklist: - [x] Add new endpoint POST /v1/playbooks/:id/checkpoint (incident-bot) - [x] CLI skeleton + replay safety gates - [x] Unit tests for sanitizers and TTL logic - [x] Integration test that uploads a checkpoint and performs dry-run replay against a local simulator - [x] RBAC checks and audit log entries - [x] Docs: section in oncall-runbooks.md and quick CLI examples

Testing/CI: Unit tests added (~120 new assertions). Integration test spawns a local http simulator and verifies that replay --dry-run does not call the simulator; interactive mode calls only after explicit confirmation mocked in tests. CI initially flaked on SLO toolkit prefetch stub; added retry logic and flaky-test marker. Final CI: 1 failing flake fixed, all checks passing on re-run.

Rollout plan: Feature is behind a runtime flag `enable_playbook_checkpoints`. Default off for Hosted; enabled for self-hosted dogfood clusters. Migration: no DB schema changes; uses ephemeral attachments only. Docs and runbook guidance coordinated with SRE docs owner.

Related linear tasks: ENG-5123 (playbook checkpoint lifecycle), SRE-234 (oncall tool safety review).
